findings.where: First screen, the action row: the 'Write to me' button and the underlined address beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The parts map shows the page's one way to reach Mark does nothing. 'Write to me' is drawn as a filled blue button and the address is underlined like a link, but neither acts. The only working mail link is in the footer, several screens below.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided to get in touch. They click the button or the address on the first screen, nothing happens, and they may conclude the site is broken or abandoned. That breaks the brief's 'one direct, personal way to reach him'.

findings.where: First screen, the action row: the 'Book a consultation' button beside 'Write to me' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: A second filled primary button has the same weight as the first, so the screen has two competing actions. Its label also offers a booked, sold service that nothing else on the page supports, and it links to #consult, an anchor no section on the page provides. On the phone it is also indented away from the column's left edge and crowded under the address.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark, because the brief asks for one action and calls 'salesy' a failure. Visitors, because they cannot tell whether to email or book, and booking leads nowhere.

findings.where: First screen, the first-person paragraph under the heading ('I ADVISE MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS…')
findings.fault: Four lines of running prose are set in bold, widely letter-spaced capitals. It is hard to read, it shouts beside the quiet serif voice, and it reads as the tracked techy capitals the brief bans. This is the paragraph that says who he is and who he serves, so the visitor works hardest at the most important line.
findings.who_objects: Bank staff skimming to learn what Mark does. Also the founder, whose brief asks for a short first-person paragraph in a serif text column, nothing 'in-your-face techy', and refined rather than loud.

findings.where: First screen ground: the hero band's pale blue-to-lavender gradient (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The hero sits on a blue-to-violet gradient band that is not in the palette. The page's own palette tile says 'three colours, no accent' and 'the paper is a flat warm tone'. The violet takes the page away from the house blue and grey and gives the hero a slick, generic tech-template look. On the phone the band also ends abruptly on a hard edge above a stretch of empty paper.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for a warm paper ground, the house blue and grey as the only ink, and nothing slick. Mark, because a tinted SaaS gradient is a look any consultancy could own.

findings.where: First screen margin notes (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024 with talk titles), and the blue section labels below the fold (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: These notes are set in the house blue, the colour the palette tile itself reserves for links and the action. Each pairs a title with a venue and year, like a list of linked talks, but none of them is a link. A visitor who clicks a talk title to read it gets nothing.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who wants evidence of his work. The talk titles look like the way in, and the dead click costs trust. The house rule reserves the link colour for links. The brief asked for blue notes, so this clash goes to the founder.

findings.where: Header lockup: the mark with 'MMM INFRA' beside the name 'Mark M. Moseley' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The logo comes first and is visually larger, and the name sits after it in small type. On desktop the 'MMM INFRA' lettering also sits right against the top edge of the hero band, so the lockup looks cramped and nearly clipped.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose personal-advisor test asks that his name lead, with the logo beside it. A first-time visitor reads the firm mark before the person.

findings.where: Article specimen, the document row's pill-shaped outlined 'Download' button, against the square-cornered filled buttons in the hero
findings.fault: The page's buttons use two unrelated shapes: a rounded capsule in the article and sharp rectangles in the hero. They do not read as one system.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will publish more document rows and needs one button pattern to follow. Also a visitor, who sees the page's buttons as unrelated parts.

findings.where: Article specimen, the photo caption (italic serif caption followed by a smaller sans placeholder note on the same line, desktop)
findings.fault: Two faces and sizes run together on one line, and the wrap drops to a loose second line, so the caption looks uneven. That works against the brief's point that captions sit on a steady rhythm.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked the specimen to prove that the type rhythm holds when Angélique adds an image with a caption.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the 'Replay the entrance' control
findings.fault: A button that acts in place is styled as an underlined link.
findings.who_objects: Few would notice. A careful reader might expect it to go somewhere, but this is only a specimen control.

findings.where: Motion sketch section on desktop: the curve on the left, the exhibit photo pushed to the far right edge
findings.fault: The two halves do not share a top line, and under the curve's caption a large empty block is left. The section looks unfinished next to the tidy column above it.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the tile's craft, because the gap reads as a layout slip.
